teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: An API accepts untrusted work, so budgets should limit the expensive operation rather than merely describe it.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Apply finite limits to expensive untrusted operations, including input size, result count, operation duration and costly concurrent work rather than accepting unrestricted resource consumption.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Enforce an actual body-byte limit with maintained middleware and constrain caller-selected batch or page sizes with Field bounds rather than trusting claimed sizes. Configure finite dependency timeouts and a supplied Uvicorn --limit-concurrency budget where the service policy needs to bound concurrent accepted work. Test an input within the supplied budget and one beyond it, asserting that excess work is rejected before the expensive operation and accepted work retains the intended contract.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Apply the supplied body-byte budget with maintained middleware and constrain page or batch size with Field bounds. Use finite dependency timeouts and the supplied --limit-concurrency policy when concurrent work needs bounding. Test one input within budget and one beyond it; excess must be rejected before expensive processing while accepted work retains its contract. Claimed input size is not a replacement for counting actual bytes.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: A single limit is not every resource boundary. Consider size, result count, duration and costly concurrency under the supplied policy.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the configured body-byte limit, Field batch bound, finite dependency timeout and Uvicorn concurrency budget visible alongside passing assertions for accepted requests and rejection before expensive dependency invocation.

practice_anchor.objective: Apply supplied resource budgets to one costly batch endpoint: configure maintained body-byte middleware, bound batch size with Field, configure a finite outbound dependency timeout, and apply the supplied Uvicorn concurrency setting. Verify accepted and over-budget requests.
practice_anchor.success: An input within the supplied budgets retains the endpoint's intended response contract. Oversized bodies and excessive batch sizes are rejected without invoking the expensive dependency. The dependency timeout and Uvicorn concurrency setting match the supplied finite budgets.

live_code.required_skill: Configure resource boundaries using existing middleware, declarative input constraints, dependency timeouts and server settings; verify the endpoint boundary with integration tests.
allowed_syntax: Python imports, assignments and function calls
Field with ge, le and max_length constraints

httpx.Timeout and async HTTPX client configuration
TestClient requests using json or content
assert statements checking status codes, response bodies and dependency call counts
blocked_syntax: Database fixture setup and teardown for state isolation
Security dependencies with permission or scope requirements
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide one costly batch endpoint with its existing request and response contracts, a replaceable expensive dependency, maintained body-byte middleware with documented configuration, and explicit body-byte, batch-size, timeout and concurrency budgets. Include an observable dependency call counter and request fixtures containing only fields from the supplied endpoint.
live_code.observable_success: Integration assertions show that an accepted batch preserves the response contract and invokes the expensive dependency, while a body exceeding the byte budget and a batch exceeding the Field bound are rejected with no additional dependency calls. Configuration inspection confirms finite dependency timeouts and the supplied --limit-concurrency value.
